SB244, sponsored by Sen. Nate Blouin, D-Millcreek, failed to advance out of the Senate Revenue and Taxation Committee in a 1-5 vote. The bill would have increased the state income tax rate from 4.55 to 5.55% for the highest earners in Utah. Blouin estimated the proposal would impact about 20,000 Utahns and raise $150 million. He said the goal was to "raise revenues from folks who are doing quite well and be able to use them for critical needs." The bill would have created a refundable earned income tax credit for low-income workers and helped fund education.

Blouin has advocated for comprehensive tax reform benefiting working people, stating: "I would like to double some people's tax rates," targeting high earners while noting "the vast majority do pay their fair share." He mentioned potential thresholds of $1 million or several hundred thousand dollars a year as targets for higher taxation.
